sources.entry: LayoutKeeper - Remembers window layouts per external monitor and restores position, size and Space (macOS 26+) on reconnect, with DDC brightness keys on Apple Silicon.

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that remembers window positions, sizes and Spaces (desktops) for each external monitor and restores them when the monitor is reconnected.
summary.what_it_does: LayoutKeeper saves window layouts per external monitor, identifying each monitor by its EDID hardware data (maker, model, serial). It restores window position and size when the monitor is plugged back in, either on a prompt, automatically, or manually. On macOS 26 or later it also moves windows back to their original desktop (Mission Control Space) and can add missing desktops in shared-layout mode. It supports several named layouts per monitor, keeps the last 5 versions, previews moves before restoring, and offers one-click undo. It also includes display arrangement presets, DDC brightness and volume key handling on Apple Silicon, a Keep Awake menu with four modes, and global shortcuts.
use_cases: restore windows after unplugging an external monitor
remember laptop and office/home monitor window layouts
move windows back to their original desktop Spaces
control external monitor brightness with keyboard keys
prevent Mac from sleeping while keeping screen on
switch display arrangement without opening System Settings
how_to_run: Download the .dmg for your Mac (AppleSilicon or Intel) from Releases
Right-click the app and choose Open the first time (app is self-signed, not notarized)
Grant Accessibility permission in the setup guide
Save a layout from the menu bar or with ⌃⌥⌘S
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd LayoutKeeper, ./scripts/build.sh
stack: Private macOS APIs for cross-desktop window moves
DDC over I2C for Apple Silicon monitors
notable: Restores windows to their original macOS desktop (Space), not just position and size, on macOS 26 or later
Per-monitor layouts identified by EDID hardware data, with a shared-layout option that stores positions relative to the screen
Hardware brightness via DDC on Apple Silicon, with software dimming fallback and a sync option for the built-in display
Verifies each window move and rolls back if it did not arrive
Keep Awake menu with four modes
caveats: Moving windows between desktops uses private macOS APIs that may break after a system update; the feature is disabled automatically if so
Hardware DDC brightness works only on Apple Silicon Macs, and not all monitors, docks or HDMI ports support it
Supports one external monitor at a time; Finder windows cannot be moved to another desktop; full-screen, Split View and minimized windows are skipped
